newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate falls to 7.4/5 pct on maturity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate falls to 7.4/5 pct on maturity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fell to 7.40/50 percent from 8.20/30 previously as liquidity improved due to the maturity of a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the overnight was pulled down by banks which were cautious in their term dealings in the morning.
"The overnight fell because Bank Negara did not roll over the maturity," said a dealer with a local bank.
However, term rates were stable because the market was cautious ahead of the year's end, dealers said.
"The market is more cautious than it was previously," said the head of money dealing at a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur.
"Though liquidity has improved, the market's expectations have changed.
"Earlier people thought the rates would come down sharply in the first quarter of next year, which they think is unlikely now," he said.
Dealers said the relatively high growth in broad money supply would not allow Bank Negara to ease on its tight monetary policy, which has been in place for over a year.
"The regulators are expected to be cautious because the monetary aggregates are not yet comfortable," one dealer said.
Earlier, other interbank rates softened marginally.
Around 0300 GMT, one-week interbank rate fell to 7.20/40 percent against 7.50/60 on Tuesday, two-week eased to 7.30/40 against 7.40/50 and three-week was steady at 7.30/40 percent.
One-, two- and three-month money was dealt at 7.30 percent, down five basis points from previous levels.
Six-month to one-year money was steady at 7.35/40 percent.
"Some more maturities are coming up next week which should soften rates further," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
A further easing in the liquidity situation is expected with the maturity of two long-term government bonds for 1.1 billion ringgit on December 15.
However, the increased liquidity is also raising the demand for the 10-year bond which was issued last month. The bond's price rose to around 100.25 ringgit from 100.05.
"Because of ample liquidity, people are loading up positions for next year," said a bond dealer with a Malaysian bank.

"Moreover, there is a shortage of liquid assets in the market," he said. The dealer said Bank Negara bill yields have dropped 10-15 basis points in the last one week, which indicated a demand for liquid assets.
"The bills and bonds maturing this and next week are being used by banks and corporates to increase their liquid asset holdings," another local bank dealer said.
He said a big portion of the government bonds maturing next week was held by corporate bodies and insurance companies, who were buying new bonds to replace them.
-- Madhav Reddy (603-230 8911)
